answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and files one key-bound work log on the umber board in a gale window; the log carries a comet timestamp, so it cannot serve a second identity. Auditors recompute each log against the comet record and burn the bond on mismatch or reuse. The filing fee is 20 for the first identity and 20+6(k-1) for the kth, so the 1000th fake pays 6014; 1,000 fakes pay 3,017,000 in fees, plus 70,000 locked. A rented-log ring fails: the rented log's key and comet timestamp do not match its claimant. One honest agent pays 20 once and reclaims the bond.
